mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand for corporate goods and services, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings power and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, resulting in neutral to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 5% YoY for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
